2609.11708.title: Language-Augmented Semantic Priors for B-Spline Surface Fitting
2609.11708.paper_summary: The use of B-splines and Non-Uniform Rational B-Splines surfaces constitutes the mathematical foundation of contemporary computer-aided design (CAD) systems. Despite long-term progress, geometric kernels in traditional CAD still rely heavily on predetermined heuristic initialization for surface fitting and parameterization. Meanwhile, the procedural semantics and design intent encoded in modeling histories are largely ignored during geometry generation. This disconnect creates a gap between high-level design intent and solver-executable geometric configuration, often leading to suboptimal and semantically inconsistent fitting results. To bridge this gap, we introduce LASP, a Language-Augmented Semantic Priors framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to infer structured, solver-usable B-spline priors from procedural modeling histories. Rather than modifying the geometric kernel itself, LASP operates as a semantic reasoning layer above existing solvers. It first translates modeling histories into rich textual descriptions that capture design intent, geometric context, and functional relationships, and then uses a fine-tuned LLM to predict structured B-spline prior parameters. LASP is trained through a two-stage scheme that combines local geometric regularities with long-range contextual dependencies, producing priors that are both interpretable and semantically coherent. This approach furnishes inductive signals that direct the conventional B-spline fitting process toward solutions that more accurately encapsulate the intended design objectives and demonstrate heightened semantic coherence. Compared to traditional machine learning schemes, the experiments demonstrate that language-driven reasoning can serve as a powerful inductive bias for geometric solving, establishing a new paradigm of language-guided geometric optimization in modern CAD systems.
2609.11708.paper_summary_zh: B樣條和非均勻有理B樣條表面的使用構成了當代計算機輔助設計（CAD）系統的數學基礎。儘管長期以來取得了進展，傳統CAD中的幾何內核仍然在表面擬合和參數化方面嚴重依賴預先確定的啟發式初始化。與此同時，在幾何生成過程中，建模歷史中編碼的程序語義和設計意圖在很大程度上被忽視。這種脫節造成了高層次設計意圖與可解算幾何配置之間的差距，經常導致次優和語義不一致的擬合結果。為了彌補這一差距，我們引入了LASP，一種語言增強語義先驗框架，利用大型語言模型（LLMs）從程序建模歷史中推斷結構化的、可供解算器使用的B樣條先驗。LASP並不直接修改幾何內核，而是作為現有解算器之上的語義推理層運作。它首先將建模歷史轉換為豐富的文本描述，捕捉設計意圖、幾何上下文和功能關係，然後使用經過微調的LLM來預測結構化的B樣條先驗參數。LASP通過一種兩階段的方案進行訓練，該方案結合了局部幾何規律和長程上下文依賴性，產生既可解釋又語義一致的先驗。這種方法提供了引導信號，將傳統的B樣條擬合過程引導向更準確地體現預期設計目標的解決方案，並展現出更高的語義一致性。與傳統機器學習方案相比，實驗表明，基於語言的推理可以作為幾何解算的強大歸納偏見，建立了現代CAD系統中語言引導幾何優化的新範式。
